title: A triple-unit microfluidic device \(D3-chip) for cell migration research
protocol: Mix equal volume of SU-8 2025 and SU-8 2000 thinner in a plastic beaker.
Gently stir the photoresist mixture using a plastic knife.
Clean a 3-inch silicon wafer.
Pour photoresist mixture onto the wafer.
Dispense photoresist mixture solution on the center of the wafer.
Spin at 500 rpm for 5 seconds and then 3000 rpm for 30 seconds to get 4-μm-thick patterns using a spinner.
Heat the wafer for 2 minutes at 95 ºC using a hotplate.
Expose the wafer to UV for 6 seconds using the thin layer photomask.
Heat the wafer for 2 minutes at 95 ºC using a hotplate.
Develop the wafer for 1 minute using SU-8 developer.
Gently dry the wafer with pressurized nitrogen gas.
Cover the alignment marks on the fabricated thin layer pattern by adhesive tape.
Dispense SU-8 2025 on the wafer.
Spin at 500 rpm for 5 seconds and then 1500 rpm for 30 seconds to get 50-μm-thick patterns using a spinner.
Carefully remove the adhesive tape that covers the alignment marks.
Heat the wafer for 2 minutes at 65 ºC and then for 6 minutes at 95 ºC using a hotplate.
Align the thick layer transparency photomask on the coated wafer using the mask aligner.
Expose the wafer to UV for 13 seconds.
Heat the wafer for 2 minutes at 65 °C using a hotplate.
Continue heating the wafer for 6 minutes at 95 °C using a hotplate.
Develop the wafer for 6 minutes using SU-8 developer.
Gently dry the wafer using pressurized nitrogen gas.
Hard bake the device at 150°C for 10 minutes.
Clean the SU-8 device master using pressurized nitrogen gas and place it in a petri dish.
Mix PDMS base and curing agent (10:1 mass ratio) in a beaker using a plastic knife.
Pour approximately 40 grams of degassed PDMS onto the SU-8 device master in the petri dish.
Cure the PDMS in a baking oven at 80 °C for 2 hours.
Cut and peel off the cured PDMS from the wafer using a scalpel.
Punch holes with a 6 mm diameter puncher in the PDMS device as the inlets and outlets.
Punch holes with a 3 mm diameter puncher in the PDMS device for cell loading ports.
Clean the PDMS device surface using adhesive tape.
Place the PDMS replica and a clean glass slide in the plasma cleaner.
Treat the PDMS replica and glass slide by plasma for 1-2 minutes.
Gently bond the PDMS replica to the glass slide.
Inject deionized water into the microchannels.
Mix RPMI-1640 and 4% BSA to get a 0.4% BSA solution.
Prepare fibronectin solution in DPBS at a final concentration of 0.25 mg/mL.
Prepare a 2 μg/mL rat tail collagen type I solution.
Remove deionized water from all medium ports.
Add 100 µl of fibronectin to the outlets for neutrophils or 100 µl of rat tail collagen type I for MDA-MB-231 cells and let it flow into the channels.
Incubate the devices for 1 hour.
Remove the fibronectin or collagen type I solution from all medium ports.
Add 100 µl of 0.4% BSA to outlets and let it flow into the channels.
Incubate the device for 1 hour before cell experiments.
Obtain human blood samples by venipuncture from healthy donors under an ethics protocol approved by the Joint-Faculty Research Ethics Board at the University of Manitoba.
Use a cell isolation kit to negatively isolate neutrophils directly from the blood.
Re-suspend cells in RPMI with 0.4% BSA and incubate in an incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 before the migration experiment.
Prepare culture medium using DME/F12 medium with 10% FBS.
Culture MDA-MB-231 cells in the prepared culture medium.
Prepare chemoattractant solution at desired concentration using RPMI 1640 with 0.4% BSA.
Add FITC-Dextran to the chemoattractant solutions as the gradient indicator.
Resuspend cells in DME/F12 with 1% FBS before the migration experiment.
Load neutrophils to the D3-Chip coated with fibronectin through the cell loading ports and let cells settle in the docking area.
Add chemoattractant solution and medium to the two inlet reservoirs of each test unit of the D3-Chip to create different gradient conditions.
Put the microfluidic device on the stage of an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Image the fluorescence intensity of FITC-Dextran inside the channel to verify gradient generation.
Record cell migration images at 6 frames/min for 15 min.
Import the images to “ImageJ” to track cells.
Use “Chemotaxis and Migration Tool” to further analyze the tracking data.
Export the tracking data to Excel for further calculation of migration parameters.
Prepare chemoattractant solution at desired concentration in DME/F12 with 1% FBS.
Add FITC-Dextran to the chemoattractant solution as the gradient indicator.
Load cancer cells into each test unit of the collagen coated D3-Chip via the cell loading ports.
Wait 5 min until enough cancer cells are trapped at the cell docking area.

Add chemoattractant solution and medium to the two inlet reservoirs of each test unit of the D3-Chip to create different gradient conditions in different units depending on the need of the experiments.
Put the device in the incubator for 15 min after cell loading and gradient generation.
Capture the final cell images in the channel at the end of the assay.
Import the images to ImageJ.
Calculate the cell migration distance along the gradient direction across the gradient relative to the thin barrier channel.
Add fresh chemoattractant solutions and medium to the device every hour.
Put the device in an incubator after cell loading and gradient application for several hours.
Capture final cell images in the channels at the end of the assay for data analysis.
Import the images to ImageJ.
Analyze cell migration distance along the gradient direction across the thin barrier channel.
